newsitem.title: JAPAN: Dlr up but off highs on BOJ comments by late Tokyo.
newsitem.headline: Dlr up but off highs on BOJ comments by late Tokyo.

text.p: 0636 GMT TRADED HIGH/LOW AS OF 0600 GMT

The dollar firmed against the yen by late Tokyo on Wednesday after another day of volatile trade, but retreated from earlier highs in reaction to comments by Bank of Japan Deputy Governor Toshihiko Fukui that the central bank is mulling the timing of a rate rise, dealers said.
Fears that the interest rate gap between the United States and Japan will narrow kept the dollar's topside heavy.
Fukui was quoted by an executive of a labour group as saying that the central bank is considering the right timing to raise the official discount rate but it does not want to make a hasty decision.
"We have seen some comments on interest rates, but this is the first time that BOJ has clearly commented on rates, so it had an impact on the market," a dealer at a European bank said.

Dealers said a wave of dollar sales was detected mostly by interbank dealers, while the yield of the key 10-year 182nd JGB rose sharply following the comments. The yield stood at 2.570 percent at 0644 GMT, up from 2.470 percent at Tuesday's close.

Although the decision by the U.S. Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) on Tuesday to leave U.S. rates steady had been largely digested in overseas trade and had little to no impact in Tokyo, expectations that the U.S.-Japan interest rate gap will shrink kept the dollar's topside heavy, particularly after Fukui's comments, dealers said.

In the morning, a strong slew of short-covering mostly by interbank traders after a sharp drop of the dollar on Tuesday pushed the greenback up more than one yen, to as high as 114.50 yen by midday. Comments by Finance Minister Hiroshi Mitsuzuka also gave it further upward impetus, dealers said.
Mitsuzuka told a parliamentary committee that worries over an excessive weakening of the yen had completely disappeared.
"A stable currency market is important for the economy. Excessive strengthening of the yen as well as excessive weakening of the yen is undesirable," he added.

Dealers said trust banks, who had sold dollars for hedge purposes on Tuesday, covered their short positions in the morning. Life insurers were also said to be keen to buy dollars for yen when the greenback fell on comments by BOJ's Fukui in late afternoon. Similar short-covering by Japanese investors was detected in crosses such as mark/yen trade.
The mark firmed against the yen, rising as high as around 68.30 yen by late Tokyo. It was quoted at 67.38/41 yen at 0732 GMT, compared with 67.16 yen at the New York close on Tuesday.

But a city bank dealer said offers from exporters and some investment trust firms were expected above 68 yen to cap the mark's further gains. In trade against the mark, the dollar edged up mostly in tandem with a rise in the dollar/yen rate, dealers said.
The Singapore market was closed for a holiday, except for SIMEX and Nikkei and foreign exchange futures markets.
